body:
Groundwork milestone for first-response latency, following the review in #439 and the routing discussions in #441 / #443. Three tasks that land now, in this repo, with no dependency on the runtime-packaging work or the App-dispatch/receiver track. *(Revised: comment-adoption plumbing was dropped from this milestone as lower priority — see the deferred note at the bottom; the entrypoint task is elaborated; answer-first is now specified as the default interaction mode.)*

Measured baseline (self-hosted runners, recent runs): eyes reaction median **15s** (p90 17s); bare mentions add a full dispatch-triage agent session before any route job; explicit answers post at median **175s** (p90 311s); **32 of 39** recent successful entrypoint runs were no-op declines that still burned 20–40s of runner time each.

---

## Task 1 — Entrypoint efficiency and follow-up parallelism ([`agent-entrypoint.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-entrypoint.yml))

### 1a. Bot-sender guard on the mention branch

The broad prefilter `contains(toJSON(github.event), <handle>)` matches the agent's **own** comments — every Sepo reply that quotes a command or example re-wakes the workflow, which then boots a runner, installs the runtime, and declines. The follow-up branch already has `github.event.sender.type != 'Bot'`; the mention branch does not.

- Wrap the mention branch of the entrypoint `if:` with the same `github.event.sender.type != 'Bot'` condition.
- No behavior change: `extract-context` (`shouldSkipSender`) already declines bot senders today — this only stops paying a full portal boot to reach that decline. It removes the bulk of the 32/39 no-op waste (most were self-triggered).
- Edge case to document: this forecloses bot-authored triggers (e.g. another automation mentioning the agent). That path is already dead at the context layer, so nothing regresses; if bot-to-bot triggering is ever wanted, it's a deliberate two-layer change.
- Adjacent but out of scope: `edited`-event semantics (#437). Editing a comment containing the handle still re-triggers; that issue owns the fix.

### 1b. Early 👀 before runtime setup (REST, payload-only)

Today the eyes reaction waits for checkout → auth → provider resolution → `npm ci` + build → context extraction (~15s median, worse on hosted runners), because `add-reaction.js` needs the built runtime and a GraphQL subject ID from `extract-context`. But for most trigger surfaces, REST can react using **IDs already present in the raw payload**:

- `POST /repos/{repo}/issues/comments/{id}/reactions` (issue + PR comments), `/repos/{repo}/issues/{number}/reactions` (issue/PR bodies), `/repos/{repo}/pulls/comments/{id}/reactions` (review comments).
- Add a first portal step (before checkout): extract the body + ID fields from the event payload (`jq`), apply a best-effort live-mention check (handle regex after stripping fenced code blocks and `>` quotes — a ~5-line approximation of `mentions.ts`; full parser parity arrives with the bundled runtime in M1), then react via `gh api`. The step needs only `github.token`-level auth for same-repo reactions, or the resolved auth token if reaction identity should stay consistent — decide in implementation.
- Coverage caveat: discussions and PR-review bodies are GraphQL-only surfaces — they keep the post-setup reaction path until M1.
- Keep the existing post-extract reaction step as a no-op-if-already-reacted fallback so behavior is unchanged where the early step doesn't fire.

**Acceptance:** on issue/PR/comment triggers, 👀 lands in ≤5–8s (runner pickup + one API call); bot-authored comments start no runs at all.

### 1c. Per-comment concurrency, with write-route locks made explicit

The entrypoint concurrency group keys on issue/PR/discussion number with `cancel-in-progress: false`, and route jobs run inside the caller's run — so a second mention on a busy issue queues behind the **entire** prior run, including minutes of answer generation. Its 👀 doesn't appear until the previous run finishes.

- Key the group on the triggering comment where one exists: `github.event.comment.id || github.event.review.id || <target number fallback>`. Distinct comments then process in parallel; identical re-deliveries of the same comment still dedupe.
- **Prerequisite lock audit:** `agent-fix-pr.yml` defines a workflow-level `concurrency` group, but when called via `workflow_call` from the router, top-level concurrency of the called workflow is not applied — today the *entrypoint* group is what serializes fix-pr per PR. Before loosening it, add a **job-level** `concurrency: agent-fix-pr-<pr_number>` inside the fix-pr job (job-level groups are honored in reusable workflows). `agent-implement.yml` is standalone-dispatched, so its existing group keeps applying. `agent-review.yml` has no lock; parallel reviews are safe (read-mostly, provenance-checked via reviewed-head capture) — optionally add the same job-level pattern for tidiness.
- Accepted, documented degradation: two parallel answer runs on the same target may race on thread-state/session-bundle registration; session policy is `resume-best-effort`, so the cost is reduced continuity for one of the two threads, not corruption. Memory commits on shared branches already handle push conflicts as reported warnings.

**Acceptance:** two mentions in different comments on one issue run concurrently and each acks independently; two `/fix-pr` requests on one PR still serialize; label-triggered runs (no comment ID) still serialize per target.

## Task 2 — Answer-first as the default interaction mode

Per #441 / #443, this becomes **the** interaction model, not just a routing tweak:

1. **A bare mention always just answers.** No dispatch-triage model call, no route inference machinery on the hot path. The `Run dispatch triage` step (a full acpx session at medium effort — [`agent-router.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml), rules in [`agent-dispatch.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/agent-dispatch.md)) leaves the default path entirely. The portal becomes deterministic.
2. **The answer teaches the next step.** The answer agent — which, unlike the old triage step, has actually read the thread and repo context — ends change-shaped answers with a copyable command block:
   - `/implement …`, `/fix-pr …`, `/review`, `/orchestrate …` as appropriate, with a one-line explanation each.
3. **Optional direct-to-approval.** When intent is clearly implementation-shaped, the same answer run can additionally prepare the standard approval request (reusing `prepare-approval` and the `req-…` flow), so the user's next reply can simply be `/approve req-…` — one round trip instead of two. Gate behind a repo var, e.g. `AGENT_ANSWER_NEXT_ACTION=commands` (default) `| approval-offer`. Approval semantics are unchanged: write routes still start only from an explicit command or an approval.
4. **Triage becomes opt-in** (`AGENT_TRIAGE_MODE=agent` restores today's behavior). Keep it clearly distinct from `AGENT_FOLLOWUP_INTENT_MODE` (#441's setting for *unmentioned* follow-ups).
5. **Implement-metadata off the hot path** (severable): for explicit `/implement` on non-issue surfaces, create the tracking issue immediately from the raw request text + source link, skipping the `Generate implement issue metadata` agent step; the implement agent retitles it as its first action.

Docs: `request-lifecycle.md`, `overall-design.md` portal diagrams, `configuration-list.md`, README "How It Works" + "What You Can Ask It To Do". Tests: bare mention reaches the answer agent with zero prior model calls; `AGENT_TRIAGE_MODE=agent` restores triage; approval-offer mode posts a valid approval request; explicit routes unaffected.

## Task 3 — Faster explicit route overrides

Explicit `/implement`, `/review`, `/fix-pr` skip triage already; what they still pay in the portal is avoidable:

- **Lazy provider CLI install.** `setup-agent-runtime` installs codex/Claude in the portal whenever a provider *resolves* ([`resolve-provider.js`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/resolve-agent-provider/resolve-provider.js) sets `install_*` purely from provider choice), even when the portal will run no model step — explicit routes then burn the install (`npm -g` / `curl|bash`; 20–60s on hosted runners) before acking. Set install flags only for jobs that actually invoke an agent; the portal on an explicit route installs nothing.
- **Dispatch-first ordering.** In the router's implement job, dispatch `agent-implement.yml` *before* posting the link-back comment / labels / 👍 so the downstream run (and its runner pickup) starts as early as possible; the courtesy steps follow.
- The bigger accelerations land in later milestones and are noted here only for direction: a "portal-lite" once the runtime is prebuilt (parse + auth + ack in ~5–8s with route jobs hanging directly off it — no `npm ci` anywhere on the ack path), and one-hop dispatch straight to route workflows when the App-webhook receiver track is live.

**Acceptance:** explicit routes on hosted runners save the CLI install in the portal; implement's downstream run is created before the portal's courtesy steps run.

---

## Expected impact

| Metric | Today | After M0 |
|---|---|---|
| No-op runner waste | 32/39 recent entrypoint runs | ~0 |
| 👀 ack (issues/PRs/comments) | 15s median (self-hosted), 60–90s hosted | ~5–8s |
| Bare mention → first substantive | triage session + answer (~5 min) | answer only (~175s median), ending with next-step commands |
| Follow-up mention on busy issue | queued behind full prior run | parallel, independent ack |
| Explicit route portal overhead (hosted) | +20–60s CLI install before ack | no portal CLI install |

Deferred from this milestone: comment-adoption plumbing for the progress reporter (adopt a pre-created comment instead of always creating one). Not needed by the tasks above; it becomes a prerequisite of the M1 placeholder/fast-ack work and the App-webhook placeholder, and moves there.

Tasks are independent — happy to split into separate issues for one implementation run each.
